newsitem.title: GERMANY: German prosecutors to charge tycoon with fraud.
newsitem.headline: German prosecutors to charge tycoon with fraud.

text.p: State prosecutors are expected to announce Monday that they have formally charged disgraced tycoon Juergen Schneider with fraud related to one of the most spectacular corporate collapses in German history.

Schneider, once one of Germany's most celebrated entrepreneurs, became one of its most wanted fugitives after he vanished in 1994, leaving his empire to collapse under more than 5 billion marks ($3.2 billion) of debt.
The Frankfurt prosecutor's office said in a statement that it had completed its investigation into Schneider and would announce details at a news conference Monday.
Christoph Rueckel, Schneider's lawyer, has said his client, who is being held in prison, will be charged with fraud, credit fraud, falsifying documents and fraudulent bankruptcy.
Schneider specialised in buying and refurbishing hotels and shopping malls, purchasing some of Germany's most prestigious real estate in the post-unification property boom.
He slid towards bankruptcy because his rental income was too low to service the huge debts he took on to buy the properties.
Schneider and his wife, Claudia, were detained in Miami in 1995 after a year-long international manhunt. They returned voluntarily to Germany last February to face questioning.
